## Overview

Button is the design system's primary action control: a single-stop, self-sizing horizontal row that pairs a required text label with two independent glyph slots and an optional busy spinner. Four variant axes drive it — `hierarchy` sets visual priority, `intent` switches the whole ramp to a destructive palette, `size` scales every box metric in lockstep (min-height 48/40/32, padding, icon size and type ramp), and the Figma State axis decomposes into a single persistent `isDisabled` prop plus four platform-owned runtime conditions. `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` each carry their own visibility toggle and their own glyph reference, so a consumer can set either, both, or neither; geometry comes entirely from the single-mode `button/*` component variable collection, so there are no density or shape modes to wire, and focus is rendered by a dedicated ring rectangle outside the auto-layout flow rather than as a border. Accessibly it is one merged focus stop on all three platforms — the label supplies the name, both icons and the ring are presentational, and `isDisabled` takes precedence over `isLoading` so an inert control never reports progress.

**Variant axes.** 4 axes across 120 variants — **Hierarchy** (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Text; default `Primary`); **State** (Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus, Disabled; default `Default`); **Size** (Medium, Large, Small; default `Medium`); **Intent** (Default, Destructive; default `Default`).

## API

_Confidence: high._

> The content row renders in a fixed order: loading spinner → leadingIcon → label → trailingIcon. isLoading and leadingIcon do not compete — both can render at once, and neither suppresses the label. Accessibility precedence is isDisabled → isLoading: a disabled control is inert, so its busy state is not announced. The two icon slots are independent: each has its own visibility toggle and its own glyph reference, so a consumer can set either, both, or neither. There are no container-level (variable-mode) properties on this component; shape and density are fixed per size.

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | (string) | – | Visible button text. The design source ships "Label" as placeholder copy, not a runtime default; it is kept short so every size starts at button/min-width. |
| `hierarchy` | enum | primary \| secondary \| tertiary \| text | `primary` | Visual priority of the action within its context. |
| `intent` | enum | default \| destructive | `default` | Semantic intent; destructive signals an irreversible action and recolors every hierarchy. |
| `size` | enum | small \| medium \| large | `medium` | – |
| `leadingIcon` | instance | (instance) | `none` | Glyph rendered before the label; `none` hides the leading slot. Instance of Icon — see ./icon-plus.md, the design source's default glyph. Independent of trailingIcon. |
| `trailingIcon` | instance | (instance) | `none` | Glyph rendered after the label; `none` hides the trailing slot. Instance of Icon — see ./icon-chevron-right.md, the design source's default glyph. Independent of leadingIcon. |
| `isLoading` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Renders a busy spinner at the start of the content row and exposes aria-busy=true. Additive — the label and both icon slots keep rendering. |
| `isDisabled` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Applies the disabled treatment and makes the control non-interactive; exposes aria-disabled=true. Suppresses the isLoading busy announcement. |

## Structure

### Anatomy

```text
Button (component set · 58:202)
├─ Focus Ring (rectangle) · decorative · a11y-hidden
├─ Spinner (instance · 57:4) · referenced · a11y-hidden
│  └─ Vector (vector)
├─ Icon Leading (instance · 57:5) · referenced · a11y-hidden
│  └─ Vector (vector)
├─ Label (text) · decorative · a11y-hidden
└─ Icon Trailing (instance · 57:7) · referenced · a11y-hidden
   └─ Vector (vector)
```

_Confidence: high._ _Reconciliation: 0 auto-fixed, 1 retried, 0 unresolved._

> Size is the only dimension-affecting axis. Hierarchy, State and Intent leave every root measurement identical (crossVariant.axisDiffs / stateComparison agree byte-for-byte), so they are documented as targeted delta sections rather than as size-style column tables.
>
> Token system: every dimensional value except cornerRadius resolves through the button/* component token family (min-height-{lg,md,sm}, padding-y-*, padding-x-*, gap-sm, icon-size-{lg,md,sm}). All three variable collections (primitives, semantic, component) are single-mode, so there is no density, shape or spacing mode to add as columns — the Size variant axis is the only dimensional ramp.
>
> Anomaly — cornerRadius is unbound. 12 / 12 / 8 across Large / Medium / Small is hardcoded while every neighbouring property is token-bound. Either the binding was missed or the radius is deliberately outside the token system; engineering should confirm before treating 12 and 8 as literals.
>
> Anomaly — button/gap-sm is used at all three sizes. itemSpacing resolves to 4 at Large, Medium and Small, so the token does not differentiate despite its -sm suffix. Icon-to-label spacing therefore does not scale with the size ramp the way padding and icon size do.
>
> Anomaly — configured strokeWeight is not a border. All four hierarchies report strokeWeight 1, but strokeSemantics.painted is true only for Secondary (visiblePaintCount 1 vs 0). Implementing a border from the raw strokeWeight would add a border to Primary, Tertiary and Text that the design does not have.
>
> Width constraint — every size has minWidth bound to button/min-width (86), one shared value so a button a designer has stretched keeps its width when its Size changes (Figma keeps a resized width across a variant swap only when both variants share a default width). The default label is "Label" so even Large hugs to 79 and every variant starts at exactly 86. Longer labels still grow the button without bound, and the focus ring grows with it.
>
> Consistency — the focus ring outset is a single rule. The ring is always exactly 8 wider and 8 taller than the button box (Large 94x56 vs 86x48, Medium 94x48 vs 86x40, Small 94x40 vs 86x32 at the default width) and its focused radius is always the button radius plus 4. One implementation rule covers all three sizes.
>
> Consistency — icon size tracks the Label text box. Leading, trailing and loading glyphs are all 24 / 20 / 16, matching the Label text box at Large / Medium / Small so glyphs and text share one optical centre line. The Label type metrics themselves are emitted as structured rows in the Button sizes section and in _extractionArtifacts.typographyTable — never as prose.
>
> Composition — the component contains no FRAME nodes. The variant root is a COMPONENT whose five children are one RECTANGLE (Focus Ring), three INSTANCEs (Spinner, Icon Leading, Icon Trailing) and one TEXT node (Label). The per-FRAME coverage matrix therefore walks 0 frames and is trivially complete; there are no wrapper frames whose padding or spacing could go undocumented. No composition section is emitted — per the structure instruction a button with icons has a single primary container and does not need a layout map.
>
> Icon ownership — the three icon children are all classified 'referenced' (designer-set) and resolve to three distinct component sets: Icon / plus (55:11), Icon / chevron-right (55:5) and Icon / spinner (55:18). Leading and trailing do NOT share a glyph. Their sections document only placement (reference, size, sizing mode) and defer internals to the Icon spec.
>
> Typography — the component has exactly one distinct text element (Label), but it carries a different bound text style per size. The Label group in Button sizes therefore emits a textStyle row plus structured fontFamily / fontSize / fontWeight / lineHeight / letterSpacing rows, one value per size column, and _extractionArtifacts.typographyTable carries one entry per size so an engineer can set the type from this spec alone without opening Figma. letterSpacing is absent from the Label node and from all three resolved label styles in _base.json, so it is reported as 0 (unset) rather than invented.
>
> Known gaps — (1) The Focus Ring's absolute x/y offset is not captured in _base.json; the uniform 4 outset is stated in the notes from the measured width/height deltas rather than emitted as a row value, and could not be confirmed directly because no Figma link was supplied to this run. (2) Carried over from extraction: "Dropped 1 raw-hex colorWalk entries that lived inside crossed INSTANCE boundaries (Icon / chevron-right: 1). Tokened entries were preserved." — colour-side only; no dimensional row in this spec depends on it. No structural gaps: 0 rows in this spec are not-measured.

### Button sizes

Dimensional properties of the button root across the Size axis. Size is the component's only dimension-affecting axis — Hierarchy, State and Intent leave every root measurement identical (see crossVariant.axisDiffs). Every value except cornerRadius is bound to a button/* component token.

| Spec | Large | Medium | Small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Container | – | – | – | Variant root — a COMPONENT with horizontal auto-layout; the button has no intermediate wrapper frames. |
| ├ minHeight | button/min-height-lg (48) | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-sm (32) | Steps by 8 per size. Only Large (48) clears the 44 WCAG 2.5.8 target unaided; Medium (40) and Small (32) rely on the host to supply the remaining hit area. |
| ├ verticalPadding | button/padding-y-lg (12) | button/padding-y-md (8) | button/padding-y-sm (4) | Halves at each step down (12 -> 8 -> 4). At Large the padded content box lands exactly on the 48 minHeight; at Medium and Small the padded content box is shorter, so minHeight is what sets the rendered height. |
| ├ horizontalPadding | button/padding-x-lg (20) | button/padding-x-md (16) | button/padding-x-sm (12) | Steps by 4 per size and stays well above the vertical padding at every size, keeping the label in a wider-than-tall pill rather than a square. |
| ├ itemSpacing | button/gap-sm (4) | button/gap-sm (4) | button/gap-sm (4) | Gap between spinner, leading icon, label and trailing icon. Constant 4 at every size and bound to button/gap-sm even at Large — the -sm suffix implies a size ramp the token does not actually provide. |
| ├ cornerRadius | 12 | 12 | 8 | The only hardcoded dimension in this section. Large and Medium share 12; Small drops to 8 so the corner stays proportional to its 32 height. |
| ├ widthMode | hug | hug | hug | Width follows label plus visible icons, never below button/min-width (86) at any size; long labels grow the button without bound. |
| ├ minWidth | button/min-width (86) | button/min-width (86) | button/min-width (86) | One shared minimum at every size, so a stretched button keeps its width across Size changes. Short labels such as OK render at 86. |
| ├ heightMode | fill | fill | fill | layoutSizingVertical is FILL, so rendered height comes from minHeight and the parent's cross-axis rather than from content. |
| ├ horizontalAlignment | center | center | center | primaryAxisAlignItems CENTER — content stays centred once the button is stretched beyond its hug width. |
| ├ verticalAlignment | center | center | center | counterAxisAlignItems CENTER — icons and label share one optical centre line at every size. |
| └ clipsContent | false | false | false | Deliberately unclipped so the focus ring can paint 4 outside the button box (see Button — Focus ring). |
| Label | – | – | – | The only TEXT node in the component. Its rendered box drives the button's content height; the type itself is specified by the structured rows below. |
| ├ textStyle | label/large/bold | label/medium/bold | label/small/bold | One bound text style per size, all from the label family. The resolved metrics are broken out in the fontFamily / fontSize / fontWeight / lineHeight / letterSpacing rows below so the type can be set without opening Figma. |
| ├ fontFamily | Lato | Lato | Lato | Single family across every size, hierarchy, state and intent. Bound through the label text styles rather than set inline on the node. |
| ├ fontSize | 16 | 14 | 12 | Steps down by 2 per size. Resolved from the bound text style on the Label node (57:495 at Large, 57:6 at Medium, 57:735 at Small). |
| ├ fontWeight | Bold | Bold | Bold | Bold at every size — weight is not part of the size ramp. Hierarchy and Intent do not change it either; those axes are colour-only. |
| ├ lineHeight | 24 | 20 | 16 | Fixed (not auto) at every size, and equal to the icon box at the same size — this is the value the leading, trailing and loading glyphs are sized to match. |
| ├ letterSpacing | 0 | 0 | 0 | Not set on the Label node and not present on any of the three resolved label styles in _base.json — reported as 0 (unset), not estimated. |
| ├ widthMode | hug | hug | hug | Label hugs its text; the button's own hug width is derived from it. |
| └ heightMode | hug | hug | hug | Hugs the bound text style's rendered box. That box height plus verticalPadding is the content height the container compares against minHeight. |

### Leading icon — Icon / plus

Dimensional properties of the leading icon instance as it sits inside the button. Rendering is gated by the `Show Leading Icon` boolean (default false) and the glyph is chosen by the `Select Leading Icon` INSTANCE_SWAP property, whose default target is `Icon / plus`. The leading and trailing icons are independent properties backed by different component sets. See the Icon spec for component internals. Section name resolves against the API dictionary as {role} — {subComponents[].name} (role `leadingIcon`, canonical name `Icon / plus`); no name drift.

| Spec | Large | Medium | Small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Icon Leading | – | – | – | Top-level INSTANCE, placed between the spinner and the label in the button's horizontal flow. |
| ├ leadingIcon | Icon / plus | Icon / plus | Icon / plus | parentSetName of the placed instance — the component set, not a variant name. Constant across Hierarchy, State, Intent and Size. |
| ├ leadingIconSize | button/icon-size-lg (24) | button/icon-size-md (20) | button/icon-size-sm (16) | Ramps 24 / 20 / 16 in lockstep with the Label text box at the same size, so the glyph and the text share one optical centre line. See the Label rows in Button sizes for the underlying type metrics. |
| ├ widthMode | fixed | fixed | fixed | Square, fixed box at every size — the icon does not hug or fill, so the button's hug width grows by iconSize + 4 gap per enabled icon. |
| └ heightMode | fixed | fixed | fixed | Matches widthMode for a 1:1 glyph box; shorter than the button's content height, so counterAxisAlignItems CENTER does the vertical placement. |

### Loading indicator — Icon / spinner

Dimensional properties of the loading spinner as it sits inside the button. Rendering is gated by the `Show Loading` boolean (default false). Unlike the leading and trailing icons the spinner has no INSTANCE_SWAP property — the glyph is fixed to `Icon / spinner`. It is the first child in the button's layout, so it renders ahead of the leading icon when both are enabled. See the Icon spec for component internals. | ├ widthMode | fixed | fixed | fixed | Square, fixed box at every size — the icon does not hug or fill, so the button's hug width grows by iconSize + 4 gap per enabled icon. |

### Button hierarchy — border

Hierarchy is a property-variant axis: children, padding, spacing, radius and minHeight are identical across all four values, but only Secondary paints a border. crossVariant.axisDiffs reports strokeWeight 1 on every hierarchy because the weight is configured on all of them; strokeSemantics.painted is what separates them (visiblePaintCount 1 for Secondary, 0 for the rest). All other Hierarchy differences are colour-only and belong to the colour spec.

| Spec | Primary | Secondary | Tertiary | Text | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Container | – | – | – | – | Root button box — borderWidth is the only dimensional property that moves across this axis. |
| ├ borderWidth | none | 1 | none | none | Only Secondary paints its stroke. The other three carry a configured strokeWeight of 1 with zero visible paints, so no border renders — do not implement one from the raw strokeWeight. |
| └ borderAlign | – | inside | – | – | Inside alignment keeps Secondary's 1 border within the 40 minHeight, so a Secondary button occupies exactly the same footprint as a Primary one. |

### Button — Focus ring

State is structural rather than visual-only: the Focus Ring rectangle is hidden in every state except Focus, and its cornerRadius changes when it is revealed. Root padding, spacing, minHeight and radius are byte-identical across all five states (crossVariant.stateComparison), so this section documents only the ring. Columns use the API dictionary's runtimeCondition labels for the Figma State axis. Values are measured at Size=Medium; the size-dependent radius rule is called out in the notes.

| Spec | rest | hovered (platform-driven) | pressed (platform-driven) | focus-visible (platform-driven) | isDisabled === true | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Focus Ring | – | – | – | – | – | Absolutely-positioned overlay rectangle, sibling to the content, not part of the auto-layout flow. |
| ├ visibility | hidden | hidden | hidden | visible | hidden | Painted only under focus-visible. Pointer hover and press must not render it, and it stays hidden when disabled. |
| ├ fixedWidth | 94 | 94 | 94 | 94 | 94 | Medium reference: 4 beyond each horizontal edge of the 86-wide default button (button/min-width). It tracks label growth, preserving the same 4 outset at any width. |
| ├ fixedHeight | 48 | 48 | 48 | 48 | 48 | 4 above and below the 40 minHeight — the outset is uniform on all four sides. Large is 94x56 and Small 94x40 on the same rule, since every size shares the 86 button/min-width. |
| ├ cornerRadius | 12 | 12 | 12 | 16 | 12 | Focus raises the radius to button radius + 4, keeping the ring concentric with the corner it surrounds. The same rule holds at Small, where the button radius is 8 and the focused ring is 12. |
| ├ borderWidth | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 ring stroke, constant across states and sizes. The stroke paint is bound in every state; visibility, not weight, is what gates the ring. |
| └ borderAlign | inside | inside | inside | inside | inside | Inside alignment keeps the 2 stroke within the 94x48 ring box, so the painted ring sits 2 clear of the button edge rather than touching it. |

## Color

_Confidence: high._

> Color tokens are driven by the Hierarchy and Intent axes; the Size axis is color-irrelevant (identical tokens at Small, Medium and Large), so only Medium is used as the representative value. Container border tokens for Primary, Tertiary and Text resolve at zero opacity, so the border token is bound but paints nothing; Secondary is the only hierarchy with a visible container stroke. Secondary and Text container fills are transparent at Default, Focus and Disabled and only paint on Hover and Pressed. The focus ring always binds the single token var(--button-focus-ring); for Destructive intent its resolved value shifts from #0067E8 to the destructive red at the Focus state. Leading, trailing and loading icons are three distinct referenced icon instances (Icon / plus, Icon / chevron-right, Icon / spinner) whose fills are owned by this parent and are documented here; their fills are read independently per slot and are not assumed to be identical. No component-scoped variable mode collections, no composite (multi-layer) paint styles and no hard-coded colors were found.

### Primary / Default

| Container stroke | var(--button-border-primary-default) | var(--button-border-primary-hover) | var(--button-border-primary-pressed) | var(--button-border-primary-default) | var(--button-border-primary-disabled) | Border token renders fully transparent |
| Focus ring stroke | var(--button-focus-ring) (#0067E8) | var(--button-focus-ring) (#0067E8) | var(--button-focus-ring) (#0067E8) | var(--button-focus-ring) (#0067E8) | var(--button-focus-ring) (#0067E8) | Keyboard focus outline ring |
| Leading icon fill | var(--button-icon-primary-default) (#FFFFFF) | var(--button-icon-primary-hover) (#FFFFFF) | var(--button-icon-primary-pressed) (#FFFFFF) | var(--button-icon-primary-default) (#FFFFFF) | var(--button-icon-primary-disabled) (#A1A1A1) | Leading slot icon (Icon / plus) |

## Voice / Screen reader

_Confidence: high._

> - Single focus stop. Merge analysis of all 6 visual parts yields exactly one: the "Button" container itself. Because there is only one stop, this spec deliberately omits a top-level `focusOrder` section — every platform table is that one stop, at `focusOrderIndex` 1.
> - What merges: the "Label" text node ("Button") is the accessible name of the stop. It is never a separate focus stop. iOS merges with `accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, Android with `semantics(mergeDescendants = true)`, and the Web gets it for free from `<button>`'s text content.
> - What is decorative: "Focus Ring" (RECTANGLE, visible only in State=Focus — render it from `:focus-visible` / the platform focus cursor, never announce it), "Icon Leading" (INSTANCE of Icon / plus, gated by `Show Leading Icon#387:121`, swappable via `Select Leading Icon#387:242`) and "Icon Trailing" (INSTANCE of Icon / chevron-right, gated by `Show Trailing Icon#387:363`, swappable via `Select Trailing Icon#387:0`). The leading and trailing icons are two distinct presentational components with independent visibility booleans; hide BOTH from assistive tech (`accessibilityHidden(true)` / `contentDescription = null` / `aria-hidden="true"`). Neither is interactive, so neither ever becomes a second focus stop — do not wire a nested `<button>` around the trailing chevron.
> - What is an indicator, not an element: "Spinner" (INSTANCE of Icon / spinner, gated by `Show Loading#58:3`). Fold it into the stop's state — `accessibilityValue` / `stateDescription` / `aria-busy` — and hide the glyph itself.
> - Accessibility precedence is isDisabled -> isLoading. A disabled control is inert, so its busy state is not announced: when `isDisabled === true`, do not emit `aria-busy="true"`, do not set `stateDescription = "Loading"`, and do not set an "Loading" `accessibilityValue`, even when `isLoading` is also true. The same precedence governs the per-state tables in this spec.
> - State grouping: Default, Hover, Pressed and Focus (rest / hovered / pressed / focus-visible) share one entry because they are identical on focus stop count, semantic properties and announcement. Hover and pressed are platform-driven and never spoken; focus-visible only toggles the decorative focus ring. Disabled and loading keep their own entries because they change focus-order membership and announced state respectively.
> - Hierarchy (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary/Text), Size (Small/Medium/Large) and Intent (Default/Destructive) are purely visual axes with no screen-reader effect. Intent=Destructive in particular is conveyed by colour alone, which no screen reader announces — the accessible name must carry the consequence ("Delete account", not "Delete" styled red).
> - Focus order stability: do not reorder focus across states; keep the stop index stable so user gestures stay predictable. In the loading state the button must remain in the focus order so focus is not dumped to the top of the screen when the work resolves.
> - Announcement length: do not stuff the accessible name with the hint, value and busy state. The name stays "Button" in every state; loading rides on the value / `stateDescription` / `aria-busy`, and disabled rides on the trait / `disabled()` / `aria-disabled`.
> - Platform parity: the merge is identical on all three platforms (one stop, label merged, glyphs hidden), so there is no divergence to reconcile. The only platform-specific choice is disabled: the Web documents the native `disabled` attribute (inert, out of the tab order) and lists `aria-disabled="true"` as the alternative when the button must stay discoverable.

### State: rest / hovered / pressed / focus-visible

Grouped entry. The Figma State axis values Default, Hover, Pressed and Focus (runtime conditions rest, hovered, pressed, focus-visible) are identical on all three grouping dimensions — one focus stop, same role/name/traits, same announcement — so they collapse into a single spec entry. Hover and pressed are platform-driven pointer states that no screen reader announces; focus-visible only reveals the decorative "Focus Ring" layer (the sole element whose visibility changes across the State axis). isDisabled === false and isLoading === false throughout.

#### VoiceOver (iOS)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button" | — |
| element | SwiftUI `Button` / `UIButton` | Use the native control so the button trait, activation and Full Keyboard Access come for free. |
| accessibilityLabel | "Button" | Supplied by the merged `Label` text node; word it as the action it performs, not as its appearance. |
| accessibilityValue | – | No value in this group; the value slot is reserved for the loading (busy) state. |
| accessibilityTraits | .isButton | Carries the role. Hover and pressed are platform-driven pointer states and add no trait. |
| accessibilityHint | – | Omit when the label already describes the result; add only for a non-obvious outcome. |
| accessibilityElement(children: .combine) | true on the button container | Merges `Label` and any revealed glyph into one element so VoiceOver stops on the button exactly once. |
| Destructive intent | accessibilityLabel carries the destructive wording | Intent=Destructive is colour-only; VoiceOver never conveys colour, so the label must say e.g. "Delete account". |
| Do NOT | Do not read the label twice. | The `Label` node merges into this stop's name; it must not also be exposed as its own accessibility element. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce "Icon Leading" (Icon / plus). | Presentational glyph gated by `Show Leading Icon#387:121`; set `.accessibilityHidden(true)` on it. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce "Icon Trailing" (Icon / chevron-right). | Presentational glyph gated by `Show Trailing Icon#387:363`; set `.accessibilityHidden(true)`. It is decorative, never a second focus stop. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the "Focus Ring" layer. | Decorative rectangle revealed only in State=Focus; VoiceOver's own focus cursor already conveys focus. |

#### TalkBack (Android)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button, double-tap to activate" | — |
| element | Compose `Button` | The material `Button` already emits `Role.Button`, the click action and the disabled semantics. |
| contentDescription | "Button" | Taken from the merged `Label` text node; keep it 1–5 words and free of the word "button". |
| role | Role.Button | TalkBack appends the role after the content description, then the activation hint. |
| stateDescription | – | No state in this group; hover and pressed are pointer states TalkBack never speaks. |
| semantics(mergeDescendants = true) | true on the button container | Collapses `Label` and any revealed glyph into one traversal node, so the button is a single swipe stop. |
| Destructive intent | contentDescription carries the destructive wording | Intent=Destructive is colour-only; the content description must name the consequence, e.g. "Delete account". |
| Do NOT | Do not read the label twice. | `Label` merges into the content description; do not give it its own `semantics { }` block. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce "Icon Leading" (Icon / plus). | Presentational glyph gated by `Show Leading Icon#387:121`; pass `contentDescription = null` / `invisibleToUser()`. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce "Icon Trailing" (Icon / chevron-right). | Presentational glyph gated by `Show Trailing Icon#387:363`; pass `contentDescription = null`. It is decorative, never a second focus stop. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the "Focus Ring" layer. | Decorative rectangle revealed only in State=Focus; mark it `importantForAccessibility = no`. |

#### ARIA (Web)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button" | — |
| element | `<button type="button">` | Native button gives the role, Enter/Space activation and tab-order membership without ARIA. |
| Accessible name | "Button" (text content) | The visible `Label` text is the accessible name; no `aria-label` is needed while the label is visible. |
| role | button (implicit) | Implicit from `<button>`; never re-declare `role="button"` on the native element. |
